sections.title: Lenses make many points: Pure point spectrum disproves Simon's L² conjecture
sections.abstract: The authors construct, for every dimension d ≥ 2 and 0 ≤ σ < 1/3, smooth bounded nonnegative potentials of arbitrarily small weighted L² size for which the Schrödinger operator has only pure point spectrum at positive energies, claiming a counterexample to Simon's conjecture.
sections.claimed_result: The authors' Theorem 1.1 constructs V with arbitrarily small ‖V‖∞ plus the weighted L² integrals at exponents 0 and σ, while −Δ+V on H²(Rᵈ) has spectrum [0,∞) and no continuous spectral component.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: d ≥ 2, 0 ≤ σ < 1/3, and δ > 0; V is smooth, bounded, and nonnegative. The claim refutes the higher-dimensional condition that the unweighted radial L² integral alone forces absolutely continuous spectrum.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors disclose substantial LLM assistance in developing the construction and proof and take responsibility for the manuscript; this new preprint's proof has not been independently assessed here.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Independent mathematical commentary surfaced on the claimed refutation, including explicit caution that the proof has not been independently verified; the result spans spectral theory and mathematical physics. Rank is based on a consequential author claim and visible discussion, not citation momentum.

sections.title: Aleshin graphs are expanders
sections.abstract: The authors prove two-sided expansion and linear diameter bounds for Aleshin level graphs, with explicit spectral and edge-expansion constants, and show the undirected Aleshin graphs are not Ramanujan from level ten onward.
sections.claimed_result: The authors establish a normalized spectral gap of at least 1 − 2√2/3 and edge-expansion constant at least 3 − 2√2 for Aleshin graphs, improving previous quadratic diameter bounds to linear order in graph size.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The result concerns finite-level Aleshin and Bellaterra graph families; spectral-gap constants are for Aleshin graphs, and the non-Ramanujan result applies to undirected Aleshin graphs at levels n ≥ 10.
sections.unique_caveat: The claim concerns these particular graph families, not automaton graphs generally; the paper also establishes that the undirected family is not Ramanujan for n ≥ 10.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: An independent MathDB note flags the preprint as a claimed resolution of the Malyshev–Pak expander conjecture and says it has not been independently checked. Semantic Scholar listed 0 current citations (not period gains); rank rests on the explicit conjecture-level result.

sections.title: The Critical 2D KPZ Process
sections.abstract: The authors construct a non-Gaussian distribution-valued critical two-dimensional KPZ process as a scaling limit of centred log partition functions of Gaussian directed polymers and as a renormalised logarithm of the critical stochastic heat flow.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove convergence in law to a non-trivial critical 2D KPZ field, identify it as a measurable function of the critical stochastic heat flow through a renormalised Cole–Hopf transform, and report non-Gaussianity with log-log covariance blow-up near the diagonal.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The constructions are for critical two-dimensional Gaussian directed polymers and the critical stochastic heat flow; stated joint convergence is at finitely many fixed positive times. Averaging at shrinking spatial scales yields Gaussian fluctuations.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper establishes these limits in its stated Gaussian-polymer/SHF setting, not universality for every microscopic model of 2D KPZ; the authors also disclose extensive generative-AI input.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A substantial cross-listed probability/mathematical-physics result defines a critical process and gives two linked limiting constructions. Semantic Scholar listed 0 current citations and 0 influential citations (not period gains), so the placement reflects the specific mathematical contribution rather than established popularity.

sections.title: Positive sectional curvature on exotic spheres in infinitely many dimensions
sections.abstract: The author constructs strictly positively curved exotic spheres in infinitely many dimensions, specifically dimensions n ≡ 3 (mod 4), n ≥ 11, and n not congruent to 255 (mod 256).
sections.claimed_result: The author computes an Eells–Kuiper invariant for a family of homotopy spheres and proves it nonzero for suitable choices in the stated infinite set of dimensions, hence those spheres are exotic and admit strictly positive sectional curvature.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The construction uses particular quotients of S³×S³ bundles indexed by a representation and an equivariant map; the theorem covers n ≡ 3 (mod 4), n ≥ 11, excluding n ≡ 255 (mod 256).
sections.unique_caveat: The congruence exclusions are limits of the theorem as stated; archived computations support parts of the argument but do not classify all positively curved manifolds.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The claimed infinite-dimensional existence result challenges the prior landscape described in the abstract and is supported by programs and outputs archived at Zenodo; this is a concrete geometric advance, not a readership signal.

sections.title: Fuglede's conjecture holds in F_p^d for p=2, d=8 and p=11, d=3
sections.abstract: The authors prove Fuglede's spectral-set/tiling equivalence in F₂⁸ and F₁₁³ and establish further structural results and partial classifications in F₂⁹.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove the conjecture for F₂⁸ and F₁₁³; in F₂⁹ they show every tile is spectral and every spectral set has power-of-two size, with all spectral cardinalities except 64 shown to tile, alongside further reductions.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Main statements concern finite vector spaces over the specified prime fields; the equivalence is between translational tiling and being a spectral set, with supporting computations described in appendices.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract leaves the cardinality-64 case in F₂⁹ unresolved and does not settle the conjecture across other dimensions or fields.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper addresses a known harmonic-analysis/combinatorics conjecture in explicit finite settings and supplies verification programs and extensive ancillary files.

sections.title: Conway's thrackle conjecture: a new upper bound of 4/3 n
sections.abstract: The author proves that every thrackle on n ≥ 4 vertices has at most floor(4(n−1)/3) edges, combining a computer-assisted check through 12 vertices with a discharging argument on suitable embeddings.
sections.claimed_result: For any thrackleable finite simple graph with n ≥ 4 vertices and m edges, the author proves m ≤ floor(4(n−1)/3).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A thrackle is a plane drawing in which every pair of edges meets exactly once, at a shared endpoint or a proper crossing; the theorem bounds finite simple thrackleable graphs.
sections.unique_caveat: Conway's stronger conjectured bound m ≤ n remains open; the argument incorporates Pammer's computer-assisted verification for graphs on at most 12 vertices.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The result improves a sequence of bounds on a classical graph-drawing problem, bridges combinatorics with topology, and has a small-instance computational component.

sections.title: The classification of smooth 3-fold flops
sections.abstract: The authors establish an analytic classification of smooth simple threefold flops and give an intrinsic characterisation and classification of their contraction algebras.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim an analytic classification of smooth simple 3-fold flops, together with intrinsic characterisation and classification of their contraction algebras.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The classification is explicitly for smooth, simple threefold flops; the abstract does not assert coverage of singular or nonsimple flops.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract-level source provides only a brief statement; precise classification invariants and dependencies require reading the full paper. No proof assessment is made here.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A direct classification claim bridges algebraic geometry and representation theory, addressing both geometric objects and associated algebras; the arXiv record describes a substantial 65-page treatment.

sections.title: A new lower bound for the sixth Schur number: S(6) ≥ 537
sections.abstract: The authors give an explicit partition of {1,…,537} into six sum-free sets, improving the known lower bound for the sixth Schur number by one and inducing several recursive lower bounds.
sections.claimed_result: The authors establish S(6) ≥ 537, report 131 pairwise inequivalent partitions, and derive improved lower bounds including S(8) ≥ 5372 and R₆(3) ≥ 539.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: S(6) is the largest N such that {1,…,N} can be partitioned into six sum-free sets; the paper supplies explicit finite partitions and supplementary data.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a lower bound, not an exact determination of S(6); the result improves the previously reported 536 by one.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A concrete certificate improves an extremal-combinatorics lower bound, is cross-listed in discrete mathematics, and the arXiv record supplies ancillary partitions and verification code.
